title: Treatment of cervical ectropion
what: The doctor treats a changed area on the cervix with radiofrequency, laser, cold, or a special solution. Healthy tissue grows back in its place.
why: When the changed area bleeds, bothers you, or your doctor sees a reason after smear tests and colposcopy. Not every ectropion needs treatment.
duration: the procedure usually takes 10 to 20 minutes; healing usually takes 3 to 6 weeks
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
Allergy to painkillers or numbing medicine
Any discharge, itching, or bad smell right now

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before treatment, you usually have a Pap smear, a swab for infections, and a colposcopy.

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: It is usually done in the first days after your period ends. Check with your doctor.

prepare.title: Infections
prepare.text: If the swab shows inflammation, it is treated first.

steps: You sit in the gynecological chair
The doctor inserts a speculum and looks at the cervix
The doctor treats the area. It takes a few minutes
The speculum is removed, and you can get dressed
feel: Sometimes warmth or cold low in the belly
Afterward, mild cramps for a couple of hours
after: Watery or bloody discharge usually lasts 1 to 3 weeks
No sex, tampons, baths, pools, or saunas, usually for about 4 weeks. Your doctor will say exactly
A follow-up exam after 4 to 6 weeks
red_flags: Bleeding like a heavy period: see a doctor urgently
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), severe pain, or bad-smelling discharge

faq.q: Does an ectropion always need treatment?
faq.a: Not always. If your smears are normal and nothing bothers you, your doctor may simply watch it.

faq.q: Can it be treated if I have not given birth?
faq.a: Yes. Gentle methods are used today. Your doctor will choose the right one.
Usually like period cramps. It lasts a few minutes.

reminders.text: Cervical treatment tomorrow. Bring your smear results and pads.
